source: Navin, 24 October 2026: BIE must be the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher; the book is the base and BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind, never just reading the line out.
opening_steps: a question about something the learner can see, then the name
every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps)
the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time
an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows
the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea
the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with
the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick

methods.name: Open with a question on something visible
methods.when: every new topic and every new family member
methods.example: Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
methods.note: The question comes before the name; the learner looks before they label.

methods.name: One everyday image per shape or function
methods.when: every term that names a shape, a layer or a job
methods.example: Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
methods.note: The image is from the learner's home, not from another textbook.

methods.name: The word root where it helps
methods.when: a term whose parts carry its meaning
methods.example: Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
methods.note: Only where the root really explains the word; never as a vocabulary lesson.

methods.name: Why starts from a need
methods.example: Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
methods.note: Name the need or the problem first; the structure is the answer to it.

methods.name: Contrast with the neighbour
methods.when: members of one family, and what the exam confuses
methods.example: Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
methods.note: Say what it is not, right after what it is.

methods.name: Ask and repeat the key word
methods.when: the one word the learner must keep
methods.note: A short repeat after a question is a teacher's beat, not a clipped note.

methods.name: Exam memory beats by level
methods.when: after the understanding, by the level profile
methods.example: Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
methods.note: School: a trick for every list. NEET: 'yaad rakhna' and the trap. UPSC: how the PYQ words it. Revision: one trick per list.

methods.name: Link to something already known
methods.when: a new place or a new structure
methods.example: Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
methods.note: The known thing comes first, the new name hangs on it.

methods.name: Meaning with two or three real examples
methods.when: an abstract word in the book
methods.example: Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
methods.note: Two or three examples the learner has felt; then the word.

methods.name: Open the book's adjective (Navin's example)
methods.when: a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is
methods.example: Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
methods.note: Three moves on one book line: what the adjective means, an example the learner knows, and why this tissue is there.

methods.name: Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop)
methods.when: every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named
methods.example: Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.
methods.note: The example has a place (bazaar, kirana shop, mandi, bank, factory, petrol pump, farm), actors (shopkeeper, buyers, farmer, worker, bank, RBI, government), real goods or money (sugar, onion, petrol, salary, loan, EMI) and numbers that change (₹50 → ₹65; buyers 2 → 12 → 3). The story runs the concept's mechanism step by step; the term comes after the story ('isliye ise … kehte hain'); then the book's definition; then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example must be economically correct and fit the learner's level (UPSC: the real Indian link, for example repo rate → home-loan EMI, only from the book or a dated source). The numbers are told as what happened, in a complete teacher sentence (Navin, 29 October 2026, on Money v1: 'pehle aapke paas 500 rupaye the, kiraane ke 100 diye, ab 400 bache'), never as a state report 'cash ₹500 से ₹400 हुआ' (S2-09).
methods.good_narration: pehle aapke paas 500 rupaye the, kiraane ke 100 diye, ab 400 bache
methods.bad_narration: cash ₹500 से ₹400 हुआ (a ledger's state report: never)
